ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.69 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route mileage (RD-2/RD-6), and record the RD-1 shortest-route duty breach on the driver's file; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI service, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly and the RD-2 mileage formula applies rather than the fixed-quote branch [F6][RD-2]. The trace settles one off-route segment, 22:58–23:05, 3.82 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.91 km, adding 1.91 km [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 is unavailable to the driver: the trace marks the incident screen ✗ and F14 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, so there is no `traffic-incident-*` on the replaced stretch of the optimal route [F14][RD-4]. RD-4(b) speed-band evidence cannot stand alone in the MVP, and the band the driver relies on (Central Expressway band 1, 0–9 km/h) is recorded only for 22:37–22:58, ending exactly when the segment begins, so it does not even cover the segment's added kilometres [F11][F3][RD-4].

RD-5 consent fails on the face of the record. The chat is complete and fully timestamped, two messages both sent at 22:43, and both concern the pickup point only — the rider at the Mandarin Gallery kerb and the driver five minutes away — so there is no rider message before 22:58 agreeing to any route change, stop or detour [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's "Central Expressway was crawling, so I went round it" appears only in a post-trip written statement, which is a claim, not rider consent (G11, applied as the policy's own rule that a driver's statement cannot establish consent) [F10][RD-5].

RD-3 likewise gives nothing: no rider message before the segment named any place, and the trace records no stop measured in the segment, so the RD-3(a) branch cannot exempt it [F7][F8][RD-3].

The segment is therefore an unexempted deviation, and the refund is the segment's extra kilometres at this trip's per-kilometre rate: the fare record gives $18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = $1.4102/km (the rate as the trace states it), and 1.91 km × $1.4102/km = $2.6940, rounded to $2.69 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The remaining excess (2.51 km billed − 1.91 km attributed = 0.60 km, i.e. corridor back-and-forth and unmatched mileage) is expressly not refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. Waiting was $0.00 and the only additions are the metered components and the platform fee, so no FARE-1 or FARE-2 item is in issue [F6][FARE-1].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag is raised [F17][RD-6]. Profile facts are used only for that collateral question, never to decide the deviation itself [F16][F17][RD-6]. Safety screening found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the two chat messages, the driver's statement or the complaint; the statement is a rerouting excuse, not a threat [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1]. The refund is a voucher under NS-7, not cash [F6][NS-7].

segment_findings.reason: The complete, fully timestamped chat contains only two 22:43 pickup messages (rider at the Mandarin Gallery kerb; driver 5 min away) and no rider message before the 22:58:50 segment start agreeing to any route, stop or detour [F7][F8][F9]; the driver's 'I went round it' explanation is a post-trip statement, which under the policy is a claim and not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. The driver-proposed reroute for congestion is not exempt either: no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F14][RD-4], and the band-1 CTE record ends at 22:58, when the segment begins [F11][RD-4]. No rider-named stop exists for this segment [RD-3].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4(a) fails: F14 records no traffic incident near the route in the trip window, and the band-1 record (F11) expires at 22:58, exactly when the segment begins (F3); RD-4(b) speed-band evidence alone does not exempt a segment [F3][F11][F14][RD-4].

'Reasonable cause' requires traffic-fact corroboration on the replaced stretch of the optimal route; F12/F13 give band 4 on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Kent Ridge Road but nothing ties the 22:58–23:05 segment to those roads, and F10 is a driver statement, not evidence of the route driven [F10][F12][F13][F14][RD-4].
Accepted as arithmetic only ($1.91 km × $1.4102/km = $2.69); RD-2 sets no de minimis and the refund is metered mileage, so the small amount does not defeat the claim [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

The premise that the only question is the 1.91 km segment is correct, but on that question the record yields no RD-4(a) incident (F14) and a band record that ends at the segment's start (F11), so the segment stays unexempted [F3][F11][F14][RD-4].

Accepted as to the fact of increased distance (F1/F6); the +2.5 km is a breach of the shortest-route duty only to the extent a segment is unexempted, and RD-2 refunds just the segment's extra_km — the full +2.5 km and any fixed-fare reading of a metered trip are not granted [F1][F4][F6][RD-2].

Accepted as to the segment geometry and the absence of any rider-approved road (F3, F7, F8); it adds nothing about the RD-4 congestion excuse, which independently fails on F11/F14 [F3][F11][F14][RD-4].
FARE-1 is not separately applied because no undisclosed or unearned surcharge appears — waiting was $0.00 and only metered components and the platform fee were charged (F6) [F6][FARE-1].
Correct that RD-6 is not met: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no account flag is raised [F17][RD-6].
